nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The local developer running es-view and viewing the explorer SPA in their browser. Here they open the ConnectClaude panel, pick a registration scope (this project / shared / all my projects), and click 'Add to Claude' to wire this running app into their own Claude terminal as an MCP server.

nodes.label: Claude CLI
nodes.description: The user's Claude Code command-line tool, outside the es-view process boundary. `claude mcp add` mutates the user's own MCP configuration (a project-local entry, a shared .mcp.json, or the user-global settings, depending on --scope). The es-view server shells out to it as the same OS user, so the effect is exactly what the user could type themselves.

tactical.explanation: Reached via node:child_process exec from the server. The built command is `claude mcp add --transport http event-storming "<url>"[ --scope <scope>]`. Because it runs through a shell (not execFile), a Windows `claude.cmd` shim resolves on PATH. exec runs with windowsHide + a 20s timeout; a missing binary is detected via ENOENT or a 'not recognized/not found/command not found' stderr regex and reported as { notFound: true } so the UI can tell the user to install Claude Code or run the command by hand.

anchors.note: exec(command, { timeout: 20000, windowsHide: true }) — a shell string, not an arg array
missing-binary detection: ENOENT / stderr regex => notFound

nodes.label: MCP connect command
nodes.description: The exact `claude mcp add` command the operator would run to connect this session, shown WITHOUT running it, so a human can read/copy it instead of (or before) letting the app run it. Surfaced three ways: the SPA renders it under the button, GET /api/mcp/info returns it, and the es-view CLI banner prints it at startup.

tactical.explanation: Projected from the server's in-memory runtime (runtime.baseUrl, set after the socket binds), NOT from any file. GET /api/mcp/info returns { name: 'event-storming', url: <baseUrl>/mcp, command: `claude mcp add --transport http event-storming <url>` } (adapters/http/server.ts:198-200). ConnectClaude fetches it via getMcpInfo() and displays info.command under the button (ConnectClaude.jsx:53). The `view` CLI action prints the same line in its startup banner (adapters/cli/es-view.ts:81). All three use the ACTUAL bound port (the fall-forward port if 5178 was taken), so they agree with the register write. Cosmetic drift: the /api/mcp/info `command` string omits --scope and does NOT quote the URL, whereas the command actually shelled out by the register write quotes the URL and appends --scope — the displayed command is not byte-identical to the executed one.

anchors.note: GET /api/mcp/info returns { name, url, command } without running it
info command: unquoted URL, no --scope (drifts from the executed string)
startup banner prints the same claude mcp add line

nodes.label: RegisterMcp
nodes.description: Register this running es-view app as an MCP server in the user's Claude configuration at the chosen scope, by having the server run `claude mcp add` on the host on the operator's behalf. This is the single most surprising write in the app: a browser click spawns a host-side process that runs the user's CLI.

tactical.explanation: UI -> server -> command -> gateway chain. ConnectClaude.add() (ConnectClaude.jsx:20) calls registerMcp(scope) (web/api.js:37) which POSTs /api/mcp/register with { scope }. The route (adapters/http/server.ts:202) resolves the live MCP url from runtime.baseUrl (returns 503 and calls nothing if the socket is not bound yet — see inv-mcp-url-ready), and calls the application command registerMcp({ name: MCP_NAME, url, scope: body.scope }, claudeCliGateway) (application/commands/register-mcp.ts:7). That command whitelists the scope to {local,project,user} (application/commands/register-mcp.ts:8) and delegates to the ClaudeCliGateway. The gateway's claudeMcpAdd (adapters/process/claude-cli.ts:14) builds one command STRING by template concatenation (claude-cli.ts:16) and runs it via exec — a shell string, not an argument array and not execFile. Injection surface is minimal today: `name` is the compile-time constant 'event-storming' (MCP_NAME, adapters/http/server.ts:39); `url` is the server's own runtime.baseUrl + '/mcp', double-quoted in the string; `scope` is double-whitelisted (the application command + a SCOPES Set in the gateway, claude-cli.ts:12/15) and appended only on a hit. So nothing operator-supplied reaches the command as an unescaped substring. The result { ok, command, stdout, stderr, notFound } is returned to the SPA, which shows 'Added', a 'claude not found' hint, or the trimmed stderr. No in-process state changes; the registration state lands in the external CLI's config (agg-mcp-registration is ownedBy ext-claude-cli).

anchors.note: button handler; calls registerMcp(scope) and renders the result
route: resolve url (503 if unbound), then call the registerMcp application command
whitelists scope to local|project|user, delegates to the ClaudeCliGateway
build command string + exec on the host

nodes.label: MCP Registration
nodes.description: This app's registration as an MCP server (alias 'event-storming') inside the user's Claude configuration. It has NO state inside the es-view process: its state lives entirely in the external Claude CLI's config (a project-local list, a shared .mcp.json, or the user-global settings, per --scope). Idempotency, overwrite behaviour, and exactly where the entry lands are all delegated to the Claude CLI.

tactical.explanation: Realized purely by the `claude mcp add` shell-out; there is no in-memory or on-disk representation on the es-view side (hence ownedBy ext-claude-cli). The registered alias is MCP_NAME = 'event-storming' (adapters/http/server.ts:39). The registration URL points at <baseUrl>/mcp using the actual bound port. The only precondition es-view enforces before delegating is that its own MCP URL is known (inv-mcp-url-ready); everything else about the write is the CLI's responsibility.

anchors.note: the only writer; effect lands in the external CLI config

nodes.label: Registration is refused until the server's own MCP URL is known
nodes.description: ERROR-level precondition that can reject the action: RegisterMcp cannot proceed until the es-view HTTP socket has bound and runtime.baseUrl is set. A POST /api/mcp/register that arrives before then returns 503 and NO shell-out occurs, so the app never registers a URL it cannot yet serve. (The scope whitelist is NOT modeled as an invariant: a non-whitelisted scope does not reject the command, it is silently dropped and registration proceeds without --scope — that graceful-degrade guard is folded into cmd-register-mcp and the input-safety reasoning there.)

tactical.explanation: The route computes url = mcpUrl() = runtime.baseUrl ? runtime.baseUrl + '/mcp' : null. If url is null it returns sendJson(res, 503, { ok:false, stderr:'server URL not ready yet' }) and returns before calling the registerMcp application command (adapters/http/server.ts:203-204). runtime.baseUrl is populated only inside startServer's listen callback once the socket binds (adapters/http/server.ts:233), so this guards the window between process start and successful bind. It is the one check in this flow that actually fails the command; the scope whitelist and the fixed subcommands constrain content but never reject.

anchors.note: 503 'server URL not ready yet' — no shell-out when url is null
runtime.baseUrl set only after the socket binds

nodes.label: McpRegistered
nodes.description: The app is now registered as an MCP server named 'event-storming' in the user's chosen Claude scope. The operator is told to run /mcp in Claude (restarting it if already open), then click a node and ask 'explain the selected node'. The fact holds only when the shell-out returned no error.

tactical.explanation: claudeMcpAdd resolves { ok: !err, command, stdout, stderr, notFound } (adapters/process/claude-cli.ts:22); the SPA's add() enters the 'done' branch on r.ok and shows the 'Added as "event-storming"' guidance (ConnectClaude.jsx:24-26). On failure the fact does not hold: r.notFound yields an install hint, any other error surfaces the trimmed stderr/stdout. Note that 'ok' means only that exec exited zero — the actual config mutation is the external CLI's, not observable to es-view beyond the exit code and captured output.

anchors.note: resolve { ok: !err, command, stdout, stderr, notFound }

flows.name: Operator connects their Claude terminal from the explorer
flows.summary: In the explorer's ConnectClaude panel the operator picks a scope and clicks 'Add to Claude'. The SPA POSTs /api/mcp/register; the server resolves its own live MCP URL (503 if the socket is not yet bound), whitelists the scope, and shells out `claude mcp add --transport http event-storming "<url>/mcp" [--scope <scope>]` on the host as the same OS user. On success the app is registered as an MCP server in the user's Claude config and the operator is told to run /mcp. The intent is one-click wiring of the running app into the user's Claude terminal, but the mechanism (a browser click spawning a host process that runs the user's CLI) is the single most surprising write in the app and the highest-privilege UI action.
flows.trigger: Operator clicks 'Add to Claude' in the ConnectClaude panel (scope dropdown local/project/user). Reachable end to end: ConnectClaude.jsx:20 -> api.js:37 -> adapters/http/server.ts:202 -> application/commands/register-mcp.ts:7 -> adapters/process/claude-cli.ts:18.
